purpose: Every numerical claim published by SaralPrivacy must have a record here. No source id, no statistic. A claim's METRIC DEFINITION is part of its identity — 'PwC 82%' is not a source, because PwC's 2024 consumer work carries at least two different 82% figures measuring different things.

approved_wording: 82% of Indian consumers say protecting personal data is a crucial factor in earning their trust.
82 out of 100 Indian consumers say protecting their personal data matters when deciding whom to trust.
PwC India's Voice of the Consumer Survey 2024 found 82% of Indian consumers say protecting personal data is a crucial factor in earning their trust.
claims.source: PwC India, Voice of the Consumer Survey 2024 — India perspective
claims.metric_definition: Share of respondents identifying protection of personal data as one of the most crucial factors in earning/building trust.
claims.notes: ⚠️ A DIFFERENT PwC 82% exists in the same body of work — social-media advertising influencing purchases. Never cite as 'PwC — 82%'; always carry the metric definition. Say consumers, not 'Indians' — the sample is consumers, not the population.

approved_wording: 40% of Indian SMEs surveyed experienced a cyber incident in the previous 24 months.
40 out of every 100 Indian small businesses surveyed had a cyber incident in the last two years.
claims.source: Tata Tele Business Services & CyberMedia Research, SME Digital Insights 2026
claims.sample: Indian SMEs surveyed (n not recorded — confirm before reuse)
claims.metric_definition: Share of surveyed Indian SMEs reporting a cyber incident in the previous 24 months. ⛔ This is NOT 'share of attacks that target SMEs' — a different metric entirely.
claims.notes: Replaces the retired Accenture-2019 43% claim. Current as of Sept 2026 and India-specific, which the retired claim was not.

approved_wording: Only 28% of Indian SMEs surveyed made structural cybersecurity improvements after an incident.
claims.source: Tata Tele Business Services & CyberMedia Research, SME Digital Insights 2026
claims.sample: Indian SMEs surveyed (n not recorded — confirm before reuse)
claims.metric_definition: Share of surveyed Indian SMEs that implemented structural cybersecurity improvements following an incident.

approved_wording: Only 12% of Indian SMEs surveyed continuously monitor their cybersecurity environment.
claims.source: Tata Tele Business Services & CyberMedia Research, SME Digital Insights 2026
claims.sample: Indian SMEs surveyed (n not recorded — confirm before reuse)
claims.metric_definition: Share of surveyed Indian SMEs that continuously monitor their cybersecurity environment.

retired.retired_wording: 43 out of every 100 cyberattacks in India hit small businesses.
retired.why_retired: Materially mislocalised. The 43% figure traces to 2019 Accenture research on cyberattacks WORLDWIDE, not attacks in India; Indian reporting describes it as worldwide. Someone turned '43% globally' into '43% in India' — an unsupported extrapolation. It is also seven years old.

retired.retired_wording: Over 40% of Indian small businesses never recover after a data attack.
retired.why_retired: No credible primary Indian study supports it. It belongs to the recycled family of '50%/60% of small businesses close within six months of a cyberattack' claims. The National Cybersecurity Alliance has formally stated the 60% figure was not generated from NCSA research and that it cannot verify the original source, and recommends against its continued use. It propagated into otherwise authoritative NIST and SEC material — which is exactly why a percentage in a reputable-looking document is not a source. Do not downgrade the number; delete the claim.
